title: Exploring the potential of artificial intelligence tools in educational measurement and assessment
venue: EURASIA Journal of Mathematics, Science and Technology Education
extended_summary:
This paper examines how artificial intelligence, especially large language models such as ChatGPT and related NLP-based systems, can be used across the educational measurement and assessment process. Rather than evaluating a specific intervention experimentally, the article offers a conceptual review of AI applications in test purpose specification, blueprint development, item generation, test instructions, item selection, administration, scoring, interpretation, appraisal, and reporting.

The paper is framed around classroom assessment and broader educational measurement, with examples drawn from a variety of AI tools used by teachers, assessment specialists, and institutions. It discusses how AI may support personalized feedback, automate grading, identify learning difficulties, and improve efficiency in assessment workflows. The authors also emphasize that teachers remain essential for design, interpretation, feedback, and ethical oversight.

A major focus of the paper is the limitations and risks of AI in assessment. The authors highlight concerns including bias, lack of transparency, privacy issues, limited human interaction, limited scope for higher-order or affective/psychomotor skills, inadequate training, technical difficulties, and possible overreliance on AI. They argue that AI can improve assessment practices only if it is implemented with human oversight, stakeholder involvement, and ethical safeguards.
quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative review/opinion-style article rather than a primary empirical study, RCT, or meta-analysis. It discusses potential applications and risks of AI in assessment but reports no original data or comparative effect estimates.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper suggests potentially meaningful benefits for assessment efficiency and institutional decision-making, but these are conceptual rather than measured. Impact is therefore unclear/modest in evidence terms, with no demonstrated effect sizes.

interventions.use_case: Conceptual review of large language models such as ChatGPT/Bard for classroom assessment tasks, including test purpose specification, blueprinting, item generation, instructions, item assembly, administration support, scoring, interpretation, analysis, and reporting.
AI-generated feedback on student written responses and assessment results, including automated essay scoring, grammar/syntax feedback, and interpretive feedback for test performance.
Using AI/learning analytics to analyze student attendance, engagement, and performance data to flag at-risk learners and support targeted intervention.
Broader AI-enabled assessment and computer-based testing platforms used to administer online assessments, monitor progress, and deliver immediate feedback.

finding.finding_summary: The paper argues that AI tools can automate multiple assessment tasks—item generation, scoring, reporting, and administration—thereby saving teacher time and reducing workload. No original effect size or sample size is reported because this is a review article; the claim is conceptual rather than empirical.
finding.measure: Teacher workload, speed/efficiency of assessment tasks

finding.finding_summary: The article states that automated grading and scoring systems can provide immediate feedback and reduce the burden of marking essays and other assignments. This is presented as a general benefit of AI-powered feedback systems, but the paper does not report empirical estimates such as d or n.
finding.measure: Grading speed, scoring efficiency, feedback turnaround time

finding.finding_summary: The review emphasizes that AI could improve assessment accuracy, consistency, and data-driven decision-making, but it also highlights major risks including bias, privacy concerns, lack of transparency, inadequate training, and unequal access. Because no empirical comparison is reported, the overall effect at the institutional level is best characterized as mixed and contingent on governance and implementation.
finding.measure: Assessment system quality, fairness, transparency, privacy, institutional adoption
